assessment_summary: Step 0003 contains two distinct flaws. First, the justification for DNF-SAT being in L ("by assigning variables to satisfy the first disjunct") is incorrect because the first disjunct may be unsatisfiable (e.g., if it contains both $x$ and $\neg x$) while a subsequent disjunct is satisfiable. An algorithm would need to check potentially all disjuncts for contradictory literals, not just the first one. Second, the implication "if it is NP-complete, then L=NP" is false under the standard definition of NP-completeness using polynomial-time Karp reductions. A polynomial-time reduction from an NP-complete problem to a problem in L only implies P=NP, not L=NP, because the reduction itself might require polynomial time and space.
